don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

* don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

* modify _manifest in place to avoid chance of unnecessary copy

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

* don't preallocate the string index mapping table either: it is
built from the RLE runs as they are read, so it grows to however
many indices the runs contain, and the string indices read from the
file are checked against the table as built

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Two independent checks are added, since either alone leaves the other
failure mode reachable:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value. This does
  *not* impose an absolute size ceiling: OpenEXR places no fixed limit
  on data size by default (see `Header::setMaxImageSize()`, which is
  off/unlimited unless an application opts in), so a legitimate manifest
  may be arbitrarily large provided the file actually contains that much
  compressed data.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, exactly as the adjacent
  `readStringList()` already does for its own reads. This is the fix
  that actually matters for the null/overread cases, since `init()` is
  reachable directly through the public `IDManifest(const char*, const
  char*)` constructor without ever passing through the size check above.

While auditing `init()` for the above, the string index read from the
file for each component of an ID entry was also tightened: it is now
validated against the string list it indexes (`stringList.size()`),
rather than against the mapping table. The index is a file-provided
value that selects a string from the list; the mapping table is just a
reordering of the same set of indices, so the list is the table the
value must be checked against.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

Verified by regenerating the reporter's PoC files (declared sizes of
512 MiB, 0, and 1) against `exrmanifest`: all are now rejected with a
clean exception instead of crashing or being killed by the OOM killer.
Also verified that a legitimate, honestly-compressed 300 MB manifest is
still accepted. The existing `testIDManifest` suite, which round-trips
legitimate manifests up to ~44 MB decoded, continues to pass.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Sonnet 5)

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

coupling:
The defect is carried by two commits that both edit IDManifest::init() in src/lib/OpenEXR/ImfIDManifest.cpp: d6f75dc4 (#2575, older) and 38d9cbf4 (#2572, newer). The patches below are the amendments applied in place to those commits, in branch order (the second patch applies on top of the first). Neither edited diff is defective on its own, and the memory error is unreachable from either commit alone:

- Original batch (no edits): the PoC manifest parses successfully, exit 0, no sanitizer report.
- Only d6f75dc4 edited: the mapping table is grown by the RLE runs and the string index is validated against mapping.size(), i.e. against the table that is actually indexed; the PoC is rejected with a clean InputExc ("Bad string index in IDManifest"), exit 0.
- Only 38d9cbf4 edited: the amendment is vacuous - it rewrites a comparison that only differs because of the first edit, so the tree is bit-identical to the original batch (the patch does not even apply without the first edit) and the PoC parses cleanly.
- Both edits (the resulting maint-batch tree): ASan heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 4, in Imf_4_0::IDManifest::init at the 'stringList[mapping[stringIndex]]' line, reached through the public IMF_EXPORT constructor Imf::IDManifest(const char*, const char*).

How the halves compose. Upstream, the string-index mapping table is pre-sized to the string list ('vector<int> mapping (stringList.size())'), so mapping.size() == stringList.size() always holds and validating a file-provided string index against stringList.size() transitively protects mapping[stringIndex]. d6f75dc4's edit ("don't preallocate") removes that pre-sizing in keeping with the commit's stated maintenance: the table is now built with push_back from the RLE runs as they are read, so a manifest whose runs cover only part of the string indices produces a smaller mapping table. The same commit consistently re-targets the string-index validation from stringList.size() to mapping.size() - which is exactly what keeps this first commit's tree memory-safe and makes the diff read as correct, self-consistent maintenance (legitimate manifests written by IDManifest::serialize() always cover every index, so testIDManifest passes unchanged). 38d9cbf4's edit ("Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read"), added while auditing init()'s validation of file-provided values, then re-targets that same validation back to stringList.size(), on the stated rationale that the index selects a string from the string list and the mapping table is "just a reordering of the same set of indices". That rationale silently assumes the pre-sized table that existed before the first edit; after it, the two sizes are decoupled, so an index that passes the stringList bound can address mapping out of bounds: stringList[mapping[stringIndex]] with stringIndex < stringList.size() but stringIndex >= mapping.size() is an unchecked vector<int> operator[] read past the push_back-allocated buffer (the PoC: 8 strings, a single RLE run [0,0], one ID-table entry whose component references string index 5 -> 4-byte read 16 bytes past a 4-byte heap block).

Why a correct fix must reason across both commits. The unsafe state is a size mismatch between two containers whose sizes were coupled upstream and were decoupled/resynchronized by different commits: the first commit changes the producer (mapping's construction) and correctly adjusts the only consumer to match; the second commit changes the consumer back to the upstream bound, which is only sound for the producer state that the first commit removed. Reviewed in isolation, each diff is defensible - d6f75dc4's tree validates against the table it indexes, and 38d9cbf4's diff merely restores the upstream comparison with a plausible rationale - and neither diff contains an out-of-bounds access; the access only becomes reachable when both land. Repairing either commit's lines without the other's context either reintroduces the hole or rejects the other commit's intent: the durable fix must restore the coupling, either by bounding the index with mapping.size() (the invariant the first commit established) or by making the table cover every index again (the invariant the second commit's rationale assumed).

pocs.entry_point: Imf::IDManifest(const char* data, const char* endOfData) public constructor (compile as C++ against the public Imf headers, e.g. g++ -std=c++17 probe.c -lOpenEXR); it feeds an 80-byte serialized ID manifest blob, the untrusted-input format of an EXR file's idManifest attribute, to the library's manifest parser
